summary: Retested the fixes from iteration 6. All of them are verified. (1) Login lockout is now per account: after 5 failures the 6th attempt returns 429, also with a spoofed X-Forwarded-For or X-Real-IP, with the correct password, and with an uppercase email; other accounts are not affected. (2) sanitize_state rejects MQTT payloads published to the real HiveMQ topic that have 1 chamber, 0 chambers, or 3 duplicate ids; GET state always showed ids (0,1,2) and the fake temp 99 never leaked. (3) Password change bumps tv: the old access token (sent as cookie and as Bearer) and the old refresh token return 401, a second parallel session is revoked, and the current session gets new cookies and keeps working (me and refresh return 200). Also checked on admin, and the admin password was restored. (4) events?limit=10000000 returns at most 500 items and limit=-5 returns 200; history?hours=99999 returns the same data as 24h. (5) UI: the user trash icon opens window.confirm('Usunąć użytkownika ...?'); dismissing keeps the user (UI and API), accepting deletes it. Regression: admin login, live dashboard data (390x844), viewer and operator 403s, logout. Full previous suites: 84 of 86 pass. The 2 failures are the known flaky timing tests (test_manual_mode_and_vent_gradual, test_vent_in_auto_ignored_by_plc); both passed on re-run.

minor.issue: With a lockout keyed on email alone, anyone can lock a known account (e.g. admin@chlewnia.pl) out for 15 minutes by sending 5 wrong passwords. This is a targeted denial of service and the trade-off of the fix. Option: keep the per-email counter but on lockout require a delay or backoff instead of a hard block, or allow login from the request.client.host / proxy-appended IP that last succeeded.

There is no TTL index, so records for unknown or nonexistent emails pile up forever (an attacker can fill the collection with random emails). Add a TTL index on 'last' (e.g. expireAfterSeconds=LOCK_MIN*60).

issues: The role picker is a native <select>, which is inconsistent with the rest of the styled UI (minor)
